- A QIP was raised in FY26 - the cash flow shows "Increase in Share Capital Including Premium 8,000" Mn with share issue expenses of Rs 159 Mn - and is being deployed into automation and debt reduction; share capital rose to Rs 494 Mn (FY26) from Rs 227 Mn (FY25) and Other Equity to Rs 40,389 Mn from Rs 28,694 Mn.

- Dominant domestic position with over 55% market share in Indian industrial packaging and market leadership in 9 out of 11 countries of operation

bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Polymer raw-material price volatility — Continuing geopolitical tensions in West Asia and the ongoing Russia-Ukraine conflict drove volatility in polymer prices through the year; as a polymer converter the Company's input cost base is directly exposed, and it relies on a balanced sourcing policy and risk-mitigation measures to manage this.
- Freight cost and supply-chain disruption — The same geopolitical backdrop drove volatility in freight costs; with a manufacturing presence in 11 countries and exports to 66 countries, the Company's logistics-intensive industrial packaging business is structurally exposed to shipping cost and route disruption.
- Foreign exchange volatility — Foreign exchange rates were volatile through the year. With 35% of consolidated revenue from overseas and international operations and manufacturing entities across UAE, Bahrain, Saudi Arabia, Egypt, Thailand, Taiwan, Indonesia, Malaysia, Vietnam and the USA, currency movement affects both translated earnings and cross-border sourcing.
- Geopolitical and macroeconomic uncertainty — The Middle East conflict is adversely affecting energy-importing and vulnerable economies and global growth is projected at only 3.0% in 2026, while global headline inflation is expected to rise to 4.7% in 2026; management also notes that amid geopolitical uncertainties it is exploring alternative LPG distribution arrangements.
- Regulatory and ESG pressure on plastics — Stricter ESG standards and regulations on single-use plastics present challenges to the industry, and the Company's Extended Producer Responsibility and Post-Consumer Recycled compliance obligations require continued investment in recycling infrastructure and product redesign.
- Product approval and certification dependency — The composite cylinder franchise depends on regulatory clearances such as PESO approval, Bureau Veritas third-party approval, CPRI certification and BIS fire-rating standards; higher-capacity 250-litre and 350-litre CNG cylinders remain subject to approvals still being pursued, so growth in the value-added portfolio is gated by regulators.
- Execution risk on the expansion and acquisition programme — The Company is simultaneously commissioning and ramping the Morai composite cylinder facility, rolling out multiple TEPL recycling plants, establishing steel drum manufacturing in Sharjah, integrating the Systoverse acquisition and completing the NED Energy amalgamation, so returns depend on delivering commissioning, ramp-up and integration to plan.
- Dependence on government programmes and public tenders — Demand in the PE pipes and LPG cylinder segments is materially linked to public programmes such as Jal Jeevan Mission, PMAY-Urban, the Smart Cities Mission and procurement by public-sector Oil Marketing Companies, so order flow depends on continued government spending, approvals and tender outcomes.

business.body: Time Technoplast manufactures technology-driven polymer and composite products spanning industrial packaging solutions, material handling, composite gas cylinders, infrastructure and construction products, lifestyle products and automotive components. outlook.body: During FY2025-26 the Group commissioned its fully automated composite-cylinder facility at Morai, Gujarat with annual capacity of 1,080 CNG cascades, equivalent to approximately 65,000 cylinders; the facility consolidates the earlier Daman capacity and provides greater production efficiency, capacity utilisation and scalability, positioning the Company to serve automotive OEM demand. Time Ecotech Private Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary, commissioned its first greenfield recycling facility at Bhilad near Vapi, Gujarat with an annual capacity of 12,000 metric tonnes for captive consumption, the first of three planned recycling plants across India; operations there will be scaled up and two further recycling facilities established. Backed by a long-term investment of approximately Rs 120 crore, TEPL will establish four fully automated recycling plants across India's West, North, South and East regions, which over the next three years are expected to process up to 60,000 metric tonnes of post-consumer plastic waste annually. Separately the Company proposes a fully automated polymer reprocessing facility at Umbergaon, Valsad, Gujarat with an annual processing capacity of 15,000 metric tonnes at an estimated capital outlay of Rs 25 crores. In the PE pipes segment capacity expansion at Gummidipoondi has been completed. Internationally, Time Technoplast through its wholly owned subsidiary Elan Incorporated FZE established Elan Steel Containers (FZC) in the Sharjah Airport Free Zone, UAE, marking the Group's foray into steel drum manufacturing in the Middle East, with the facility built to international standards and equipped with advanced automation and stringent quality control systems; projected volume growth is over 15% per annum over the next three years. The Group is developing higher-capacity 250-litre and 350-litre CNG cylinders and a 14.2-kg LPG cylinder, and is pursuing approvals for the higher-capacity CNG variants, while continuing to advance its composite-cylinder portfolio through PESO-approved hydrogen solutions and new products for CNG, fuel-cell and drone applications; manufacturing consolidation, brownfield expansion and new capacity additions are expected to improve efficiency and support global growth. On the inorganic side, the Company acquired a 76% equity stake in Systoverse Private Limited, a Maharashtra-based manufacturer of ISI-certified HDPE pipes and sprinkler systems under the brand 'Systo', on June 10, 2026, with total projected investment including plant upgradations, modernization, capex for plant and machinery and capacity expansion of approximately Rs 250 Mn. The energy storage business is being consolidated through the approved amalgamation of NED Energy Limited into Power Build Batteries Private Limited with an appointed date of April 1, 2024. On the energy side, Power Purchase Agreements for renewable energy across Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Gujarat and West Bengal have commenced generating annualised benefits of approximately Rs 11 Crore, with additional benefits from Maharashtra and Uttarakhand expected from Q3 FY27 and an estimated payback period on equity investment of approximately one year; the Company targets 75% of total power consumption from green energy sources within the next two years through expanded rooftop solar and group captive solar arrangements. The Company operates 24 manufacturing plants and 8 offices in India and has a manufacturing presence in 11 countries.

outlook.body:
- The outlook for industrial packaging remains favourable, led by growth in specialty chemicals, FMCG, food products, paints, pharmaceuticals and construction chemicals
- India's cost competitiveness, skilled workforce and expanding chemical-manufacturing capacity are encouraging global companies to diversify production and supply chains across Asia, with India a preferred sourcing destination under the China+1 strategy
- Rising chemical exports, continued domestic capacity additions, infrastructure investment and the gradual substitution of metal packaging with lightweight and cost-effective polymer alternatives are expected to support sustained demand for industrial packaging
- The Company remains optimistic about the medium-term outlook for the PE pipes segment, supported by a healthy order book, new product introductions and continued public investment in water, sanitation and housing; demand is also expected from urban infrastructure, irrigation, sewerage, cable ducting and affordable housing
- PNGRB's programme envisages 18,336 CNG stations by 2034, which should drive demand for lightweight composite cylinders across CNG cascades, mobile refuelling units, commercial and passenger vehicles, intracity buses and gas-transportation applications
- The expanding compressed-biogas ecosystem provides an additional demand avenue, with 132 CBG plants commissioned at approximately 920 tonnes per day by January 2026 and further capacity under development through the SATAT initiative
- The Indian LPG cylinder market benefits from a large installed consumer base and sustained refill demand, with more than 50 crore cylinders in circulation predominantly steel, and OMCs regularly procuring new cylinders for replacement and fresh demand, supporting increasing adoption of composite cylinders
- Composite products expand the addressable market because composites are increasingly replacing metals across energy, mobility, infrastructure and industrial applications on the strength of superior strength-to-weight ratio, corrosion resistance, safety and design flexibility
- New high-technology composite initiatives are expected to strengthen the contribution of value-added products, support margin improvement and enhance capital efficiency
- Hydrogen adoption gathering momentum across transportation, power generation and industrial applications positions the Company to participate in the evolving hydrogen economy
- The global chemical industry is driving increasing demand for HDPE-bottled rigid IBCs on account of their chemical resistance, and the market share for composite IBCs is expected to grow significantly
- India's e-rickshaw base of approximately 1.6 million with around 0.4 million added annually addresses an estimated market opportunity of Rs 6,400 crore for the eSTART with Selenium battery
- India's BESS requirement is estimated by the Central Electricity Authority to increase from 34.72 GWh in FY2026-27 to 236.22 GWh by FY2031-32, indicating significant long-term growth potential for energy storage
- The Middle East continues to be one of the Group's fastest-growing markets, with active operations across Sharjah, Bahrain, Saudi Arabia and Egypt
- Capital expenditure towards greenfield and brownfield projects is expected to further strengthen the Company's operating leverage and margin trajectory going forward
- Stricter ESG standards and regulations on single-use plastics present challenges, while advancements in recycling, sustainable packaging and reusable plastic solutions help drive long-term industry growth
- The Company has an order book of approximately Rs 195 crore as of June 2026 for its Type IV composite CNG cylinders, addressing demand from CGD companies, transport fleets and automotive OEMs
- The PE pipes (infrastructure) segment carries an order book of approximately Rs 265 crore, alongside completed capacity expansion at Gummidipoondi
- Following the year-end the Group secured an HPCL contract worth approximately Rs 38.14 crore for 1.40 lakh 10-kg Type IV composite LPG cylinders
- The Group expanded into several new international markets and has submitted product samples for evaluation in Kuwait, Oman and Saudi Arabia

open.item: Power Purchase Agreements for renewable energy across Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Gujarat and West Bengal have commenced generating annualised benefits of approximately Rs 11 Crore, with additional benefits from Maharashtra and Uttarakhand expected from Q3 FY27.

The Company targets sourcing 75% of total power consumption from green energy sources within the next two years through expanded rooftop solar installations and group captive solar power arrangements across additional manufacturing locations.
Over the next three years the TEPL recycling facilities are expected to process up to 60,000 metric tonnes of post-consumer plastic waste annually.
The Middle East business is expected to deliver projected volume growth of over 15% per annum over the next three years following the establishment of Elan Steel Containers (FZC) in Sharjah.
Time Ecotech Private Limited will establish four fully automated recycling plants across India's West, North, South and East regions backed by a long-term investment of approximately Rs 120 crore.

The Company has developed 6 kg and 9 kg composite fire extinguishers and is engaging with suppliers to commercialise them, initially targeting oil refineries with an estimated annual requirement of approximately 800,000 units.

The Company proposes a fully automated polymer reprocessing facility at Umbergaon, Valsad, Gujarat with an annual processing capacity of 15,000 metric tonnes at an estimated capital outlay of Rs 25 crores.

The Company is developing higher-capacity cylinders and application-specific solutions expected to strengthen the contribution of value-added products, support margin improvement and enhance capital efficiency.

TimeTech is exploring joint ventures and tie-ups with private gas distributors for an independent LPG distribution network while continuing discussions with government authorities regarding approvals and tenders.

The Group is consolidating its energy storage business under a unified structure through the approved amalgamation of NED Energy Limited into Power Build Batteries Private Limited, expected to yield operational efficiency, optimal resource utilisation, improved profitability and economies of scale.
The Company has adopted a Dividend Distribution Policy under Regulation 43A of the SEBI Listing Regulations to determine the distribution of dividends.
Following the year-end the Group secured an HPCL contract worth approximately Rs 38.14 crore for 1.40 lakh 10-kg Type IV composite LPG cylinders.
The Group is developing higher-capacity 250-litre and 350-litre CNG cylinders and a 14.2-kg LPG cylinder and is pursuing approvals for the higher-capacity CNG variants.
Operations of the newly commissioned Bhilad greenfield recycling facility will be scaled up and two further recycling facilities will be established across India.

Following the 76% acquisition of Systoverse Private Limited, the Company's total projected investment including plant upgradations, modernization, capex for plant and machinery and capacity expansion is approximately Rs 250 Mn.

The Company proposes to establish a fully automated polymer reprocessing facility at Umbergaon, Valsad, Gujarat with an annual processing capacity of 15,000 metric tonnes at an estimated capital outlay of Rs 25 crores.
The Company will continue to consolidate and automate manufacturing operations to improve resource efficiency, reduce manpower and power costs and enhance overall ROCE.

risks.note: Continuing geopolitical tensions in West Asia and the ongoing Russia-Ukraine conflict drove volatility in polymer prices through the year; as a polymer converter the Company's input cost base is directly exposed, and it relies on a balanced sourcing policy and risk-mitigation measures to manage this.

The same geopolitical backdrop drove volatility in freight costs; with a manufacturing presence in 11 countries and exports to 66 countries, the Company's logistics-intensive industrial packaging business is structurally exposed to shipping cost and route disruption.

Foreign exchange rates were volatile through the year. With 35% of consolidated revenue from overseas and international operations and manufacturing entities across UAE, Bahrain, Saudi Arabia, Egypt, Thailand, Taiwan, Indonesia, Malaysia, Vietnam and the USA, currency movement affects both translated earnings and cross-border sourcing.

The Middle East conflict is adversely affecting energy-importing and vulnerable economies and global growth is projected at only 3.0% in 2026, while global headline inflation is expected to rise to 4.7% in 2026; management also notes that amid geopolitical uncertainties it is exploring alternative LPG distribution arrangements.

Stricter ESG standards and regulations on single-use plastics present challenges to the industry, and the Company's Extended Producer Responsibility and Post-Consumer Recycled compliance obligations require continued investment in recycling infrastructure and product redesign.
risks.risk: Regulatory and ESG pressure on plastics

risks.note: The composite cylinder franchise depends on regulatory clearances such as PESO approval, Bureau Veritas third-party approval, CPRI certification and BIS fire-rating standards; higher-capacity 250-litre and 350-litre CNG cylinders remain subject to approvals still being pursued, so growth in the value-added portfolio is gated by regulators.

The Company is simultaneously commissioning and ramping the Morai composite cylinder facility, rolling out multiple TEPL recycling plants, establishing steel drum manufacturing in Sharjah, integrating the Systoverse acquisition and completing the NED Energy amalgamation, so returns depend on delivering commissioning, ramp-up and integration to plan.

The Company operates 24 manufacturing plants and 8 offices in India and has a manufacturing presence in 11 countries.

risks.note: Continuing geopolitical tensions in West Asia and the ongoing Russia-Ukraine conflict drove volatility in polymer prices through the year; as a polymer converter the Company's input cost base is directly exposed, and it relies on a balanced sourcing policy and risk-mitigation measures to manage this.

The same geopolitical backdrop drove volatility in freight costs; with a manufacturing presence in 11 countries and exports to 66 countries, the Company's logistics-intensive industrial packaging business is structurally exposed to shipping cost and route disruption.

Foreign exchange rates were volatile through the year. With 35% of consolidated revenue from overseas and international operations and manufacturing entities across UAE, Bahrain, Saudi Arabia, Egypt, Thailand, Taiwan, Indonesia, Malaysia, Vietnam and the USA, currency movement affects both translated earnings and cross-border sourcing.

The Middle East conflict is adversely affecting energy-importing and vulnerable economies and global growth is projected at only 3.0% in 2026, while global headline inflation is expected to rise to 4.7% in 2026; management also notes that amid geopolitical uncertainties it is exploring alternative LPG distribution arrangements.

risks.risk: Regulatory and ESG pressure on plastics
risks.note: Stricter ESG standards and regulations on single-use plastics present challenges to the industry, and the Company's Extended Producer Responsibility and Post-Consumer Recycled compliance obligations require continued investment in recycling infrastructure and product redesign.

The composite cylinder franchise depends on regulatory clearances such as PESO approval, Bureau Veritas third-party approval, CPRI certification and BIS fire-rating standards; higher-capacity 250-litre and 350-litre CNG cylinders remain subject to approvals still being pursued, so growth in the value-added portfolio is gated by regulators.

risks.risk: Execution risk on the expansion and acquisition programme
risks.note: The Company is simultaneously commissioning and ramping the Morai composite cylinder facility, rolling out multiple TEPL recycling plants, establishing steel drum manufacturing in Sharjah, integrating the Systoverse acquisition and completing the NED Energy amalgamation, so returns depend on delivering commissioning, ramp-up and integration to plan.

risks.risk: Dependence on government programmes and public tenders
risks.note: Demand in the PE pipes and LPG cylinder segments is materially linked to public programmes such as Jal Jeevan Mission, PMAY-Urban, the Smart Cities Mission and procurement by public-sector Oil Marketing Companies, so order flow depends on continued government spending, approvals and tender outcomes.

one-line thesis: Time Technoplast is a global leader in polymer and composite manufacturing, replacing traditional steel packaging with lightweight, durable solutions and pioneering hydrogen-ready composite cylinders for energy transition markets.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Time Technoplast is a multinational polymer and composite products manufacturer with a manufacturing presence in 11 countries, holding over 55% market share in domestic industrial packaging and market leadership in 9 of the 11 countries in which it operates.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Time Technoplast manufactures technology-driven polymer and composite products spanning industrial packaging solutions, material handling, composite gas cylinders, infrastructure and construction products, lifestyle products and automotive components. Its established products basket covers industrial packaging (drums, jerry cans and pails), infrastructure (PE pipes and energy storage devices) and technical and lifestyle products (turf and matting, disposable bins, auto components), while its value-added basket covers Intermediate Bulk Containers, composite cylinders and MOX films. It operates primarily on a B2B model, serving over 900 institutional customers globally across more than 14 recognised brands in specialty chemicals, FMCG, construction chemicals, paints and inks, pharmaceuticals, lube oils and additives and other end-user industries.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- The outlook for industrial packaging remains favourable, led by growth in specialty chemicals, FMCG, food products, paints, pharmaceuticals and construction chemicals
- India's cost competitiveness, skilled workforce and expanding chemical-manufacturing capacity are encouraging global companies to diversify production and supply chains across Asia, with India a preferred sourcing destination under the China+1 strategy
- Rising chemical exports, continued domestic capacity additions, infrastructure investment and the gradual substitution of metal packaging with lightweight and cost-effective polymer alternatives are expected to support sustained demand for industrial packaging
- The Company remains optimistic about the medium-term outlook for the PE pipes segment, supported by a healthy order book, new product introductions and continued public investment in water, sanitation and housing; demand is also expected from urban infrastructure, irrigation, sewerage, cable ducting and affordable housing
- PNGRB's programme envisages 18,336 CNG stations by 2034, which should drive demand for lightweight composite cylinders across CNG cascades, mobile refuelling units, commercial and passenger vehicles, intracity buses and gas-transportation applications
- The expanding compressed-biogas ecosystem provides an additional demand avenue, with 132 CBG plants commissioned at approximately 920 tonnes per day by January 2026 and further capacity under development through the SATAT initiative
- The Indian LPG cylinder market benefits from a large installed consumer base and sustained refill demand, with more than 50 crore cylinders in circulation predominantly steel, and OMCs regularly procuring new cylinders for replacement and fresh demand, supporting increasing adoption of composite cylinders
- Composite products expand the addressable market because composites are increasingly replacing metals across energy, mobility, infrastructure and industrial applications on the strength of superior strength-to-weight ratio, corrosion resistance, safety and design flexibility
- New high-technology composite initiatives are expected to strengthen the contribution of value-added products, support margin improvement and enhance capital efficiency
- Hydrogen adoption gathering momentum across transportation, power generation and industrial applications positions the Company to participate in the evolving hydrogen economy
- The global chemical industry is driving increasing demand for HDPE-bottled rigid IBCs on account of their chemical resistance, and the market share for composite IBCs is expected to grow significantly
- India's e-rickshaw base of approximately 1.6 million with around 0.4 million added annually addresses an estimated market opportunity of Rs 6,400 crore for the eSTART with Selenium battery
- India's BESS requirement is estimated by the Central Electricity Authority to increase from 34.72 GWh in FY2026-27 to 236.22 GWh by FY2031-32, indicating significant long-term growth potential for energy storage
- The Middle East continues to be one of the Group's fastest-growing markets, with active operations across Sharjah, Bahrain, Saudi Arabia and Egypt
- Capital expenditure towards greenfield and brownfield projects is expected to further strengthen the Company's operating leverage and margin trajectory going forward
- Stricter ESG standards and regulations on single-use plastics present challenges, while advancements in recycling, sustainable packaging and reusable plastic solutions help drive long-term industry growth
- The Company has an order book of approximately Rs 195 crore as of June 2026 for its Type IV composite CNG cylinders, addressing demand from CGD companies, transport fleets and automotive OEMs
- The PE pipes (infrastructure) segment carries an order book of approximately Rs 265 crore, alongside completed capacity expansion at Gummidipoondi
- Following the year-end the Group secured an HPCL contract worth approximately Rs 38.14 crore for 1.40 lakh 10-kg Type IV composite LPG cylinders
- The Group expanded into several new international markets and has submitted product samples for evaluation in Kuwait, Oman and Saudi Arabia
- PowerBuild has entered into a multi-year exclusive agreement with Bulgaria-based Monbat AD to supply advanced VRLA stationary batteries in India

The Group is developing higher-capacity 250-litre and 350-litre CNG cylinders and a 14.2-kg LPG cylinder, and is pursuing approvals for the higher-capacity CNG variants, while continuing to advance its composite-cylinder portfolio through PESO-approved hydrogen solutions and new products for CNG, fuel-cell and drone applications; manufacturing consolidation, brownfield expansion and new capacity additions are expected to improve efficiency and support global growth. On the inorganic side, the Company acquired a 76% equity stake in Systoverse Private Limited, a Maharashtra-based manufacturer of ISI-certified HDPE pipes and sprinkler systems under the brand 'Systo', on June 10, 2026, with total projected investment including plant upgradations, modernization, capex for plant and machinery and capacity expansion of approximately Rs 250 Mn. The energy storage business is being consolidated through the approved amalgamation of NED Energy Limited into Power Build Batteries Private Limited with an appointed date of April 1, 2024. On the energy side, Power Purchase Agreements for renewable energy across Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Gujarat and West Bengal have commenced generating annualised benefits of approximately Rs 11 Crore, with additional benefits from Maharashtra and Uttarakhand expected from Q3 FY27 and an estimated payback period on equity investment of approximately one year; the Company targets 75% of total power consumption from green energy sources within the next two years through expanded rooftop solar and group captive solar arrangements. The Company operates 24 manufacturing plants and 8 offices in India and has a manufacturing presence in 11 countries.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Dominant domestic position with over 55% market share in Indian industrial packaging and market leadership in 9 out of 11 countries of operation
- World's largest manufacturer of polymer drums (ranked No. 1) and third-largest manufacturer of IBCs worldwide
- World's second-largest composite cylinder manufacturer offering one of the widest product ranges in the industry
- First-mover technology position: first in India to introduce PE Drums replacing steel drums, first Type-IV CNG cylinders to receive PESO approval in India, first locally manufactured Type-III oxygen and breathing-air cylinders to receive PESO approval, and India's first PESO-approved Type-III composite hydrogen cylinder for drone applications
- Regulatory approval moat: cylinders approved in over 50 countries, with the LPG composite cylinder export network extending to more than 51 countries
- Broad-based, low-concentration customer profile with no single customer accounting for more than 5% of total sales, across over 900 institutional customers and 14+ recognised brands
- Diversified end-user exposure across chemicals, petrochemicals, paints, food and beverages, pharmaceuticals, agriculture and automotive that supports resilience and reduces dependence on any single industry
- Geographic diversification across a manufacturing presence in 11 countries and exports to 66 countries
- In-house R&D and product design capability that has produced IBCs, plastic fuel tanks, lithium batteries, spray suppression systems and composite gas cylinders
- Backward integration into recycled raw material through the Time Ecotech recycling facility, supporting EPR compliance and long-term cost efficiency
- Manufacturing consolidation and automation programme aimed at improving resource efficiency and reducing manpower and power costs

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Polymer raw-material price volatility — Continuing geopolitical tensions in West Asia and the ongoing Russia-Ukraine conflict drove volatility in polymer prices through the year; as a polymer converter the Company's input cost base is directly exposed, and it relies on a balanced sourcing policy and risk-mitigation measures to manage this.
- Freight cost and supply-chain disruption — The same geopolitical backdrop drove volatility in freight costs; with a manufacturing presence in 11 countries and exports to 66 countries, the Company's logistics-intensive industrial packaging business is structurally exposed to shipping cost and route disruption.
- Foreign exchange volatility — Foreign exchange rates were volatile through the year. With 35% of consolidated revenue from overseas and international operations and manufacturing entities across UAE, Bahrain, Saudi Arabia, Egypt, Thailand, Taiwan, Indonesia, Malaysia, Vietnam and the USA, currency movement affects both translated earnings and cross-border sourcing.
- Geopolitical and macroeconomic uncertainty — The Middle East conflict is adversely affecting energy-importing and vulnerable economies and global growth is projected at only 3.0% in 2026, while global headline inflation is expected to rise to 4.7% in 2026; management also notes that amid geopolitical uncertainties it is exploring alternative LPG distribution arrangements.
- Regulatory and ESG pressure on plastics — Stricter ESG standards and regulations on single-use plastics present challenges to the industry, and the Company's Extended Producer Responsibility and Post-Consumer Recycled compliance obligations require continued investment in recycling infrastructure and product redesign.
- Product approval and certification dependency — The composite cylinder franchise depends on regulatory clearances such as PESO approval, Bureau Veritas third-party approval, CPRI certification and BIS fire-rating standards; higher-capacity 250-litre and 350-litre CNG cylinders remain subject to approvals still being pursued, so growth in the value-added portfolio is gated by regulators.
- Execution risk on the expansion and acquisition programme — The Company is simultaneously commissioning and ramping the Morai composite cylinder facility, rolling out multiple TEPL recycling plants, establishing steel drum manufacturing in Sharjah, integrating the Systoverse acquisition and completing the NED Energy amalgamation, so returns depend on delivering commissioning, ramp-up and integration to plan.
- Dependence on government programmes and public tenders — Demand in the PE pipes and LPG cylinder segments is materially linked to public programmes such as Jal Jeevan Mission, PMAY-Urban, the Smart Cities Mission and procurement by public-sector Oil Marketing Companies, so order flow depends on continued government spending, approvals and tender outcomes.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Transition from conventional technology-based products to high-technology composite solutions, expanding the portfolio across CNG, LPG and hydrogen storage cylinders, breathing-air and medical-oxygen cylinders, fire extinguishers and air-receiver tanks
- Shift the revenue mix towards value-added products (composite cylinders, IBCs and MOX films) as the foundation for higher-margin, technology-driven growth
